# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tohi_2023_nivolumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tohi_2023_nivolumab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1097/FTD.0000000000000996> (open access,
  PMC9819210)
* Supplemental Digital Content 1: Table S1 (forward covariate inclusion),
  Table S2 (backward elimination), Table S3 (longitudinal albumin and eGFR)
  and Figure S1 (Monte Carlo trough concentrations by regimen, albumin and
  eGFR).

Tohi et al. fitted a population PK model to 223 opportunistically sampled
remnant-serum nivolumab concentrations from 34 Japanese patients with
non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with 240 mg nivolumab
monotherapy in routine care. The structural model is two-compartment with
first-order elimination. Clearance depends on serum albumin (negative power
effect), eGFR (positive power effect), and a sigmoid Emax decrease with time
since the first dose whose three parameters were held at the values of
Osawa et al. (2019, gastric cancer); the data could not estimate them.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Tohi_2023_nivolumab")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
ui
```

## Structure

$$
CL_i(t) = CL \cdot \left(\frac{ALB}{3.6}\right)^{-1.48}
\left(\frac{eGFR}{70}\right)^{0.411}
\exp\!\left(\frac{-0.285\, t^{2.02}}{1510^{2.02} + t^{2.02}}\right) e^{\eta_{CL}}
$$

with $t$ the time since the first dose in hours, ALB in g/dL and eGFR in
mL/min/1.73 m$^2$. Volumes and Q have no covariates; IIV is on CL and V1
only. The canonical `ALB` column is in g/L, so the model divides by 10
internally; supply albumin in g/L.

# Population

`r ui$population$n_subjects` Japanese adults with NSCLC at a single centre
(Kobe City Medical Center General Hospital), median age 69 years (38-83),
median weight 62.7 kg (36.8-80.5), 9 of 34 female (26.5%). Histology was
adenocarcinoma in 22, squamous cell carcinoma in 11 and not otherwise
specified in 1. Thirty-three patients received 240 mg every 2 weeks and one
every 3 weeks; the median number of doses was 16.5 (1-75) over a median 296
days (14-1217). Median eGFR (Japanese-population equation) was 70
(29-144) mL/min/1.73 m$^2$ and median serum albumin 3.6 (2.5-4.8) g/dL
(Table 1). Albumin and eGFR were entered as time-varying covariates; their
baseline and last-dose summaries are in Table S3.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: two-compartment, first-order elimination | -- | Methods, 'Pharmacokinetic Analysis'; Results, 'Base Model' |
| `lcl` | log(0.0064 L/h) | Table 2, CL; Results final CL equation |
| `lvc` | log(2.28 L) | Table 2, V1 |
| `lvp` | log(1.81 L) | Table 2, V2 |
| `lq` | log(0.018 L/h) | Table 2, Q |
| `e_alb_cl` | -1.48, reference 3.6 g/dL | Table 2, theta for albumin; Results final CL equation |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.411, reference 70 mL/min/1.73 m$^2$ | Table 2, theta for eGFR; Results final CL equation |
| Covariate form `(COV/median)^theta` | -- | Methods, continuous-covariate equation |
| `cl_time_max` | -0.285 (held constant) | Table 2, theta for EMAX; Methods (from Osawa et al.) |
| `lcl_t50` | log(1510 h) (held constant) | Table 2, theta for TM50; Methods. The final CL equation prints 1501 (see Errata) |
| `lcl_time_hill` | log(2.02) (held constant) | Table 2, theta for HILL; Methods |
| Time-varying CL form `exp(Emax t^g/(T50^g + t^g))` | -- | Methods sigmoid Emax equation; Results final CL equation |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.194$^2$) = 0.03695 | Table 2, IIV for CL 19.4 CV% |
| `etalvc` | log(1 + 0.463$^2$) = 0.19425 | Table 2, IIV for V1 46.3 CV% |
| No IIV on Q, V2 | -- | Results, 'Base Model' |
| `propSd` | 0.160 | Table 2, proportional error 16.0 CV% |

# Virtual cohort

Albumin and eGFR are drawn from normal distributions with the baseline mean
and SD of Table S3 (albumin 3.8 +/- 0.5 g/dL, eGFR 72.3 +/- 20.9
mL/min/1.73 m$^2$), truncated to the observed ranges of Table 1. Table S3
shows no systematic change in either during treatment, so both are held
constant within a subject. Body weight is drawn from the normal
distribution the authors used for their Monte Carlo simulation (mean 59.7
kg, SD 12.3 kg) and only matters for weight-based dosing.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2023)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2023)

rtnorm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  while (any(bad <- x < lo | x > hi)) x[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), mean, sd)
  x
}

n_sub <- 200
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  alb_gdL = rtnorm(n_sub, 3.8, 0.5, 2.5, 4.8),
  CRCL = rtnorm(n_sub, 72.3, 20.9, 29, 144),
  WT = rtnorm(n_sub, 59.7, 12.3, 36.8, 80.5)
) |>
  mutate(ALB = alb_gdL * 10)
summary(cohort[, c("alb_gdL", "CRCL", "WT")])
```

# Simulation: 240 mg every 2 weeks for one year

The infusion duration is not stated in the paper; 30 minutes (the approved
duration for the 240 mg flat dose in Japan) is used.

```{r sim-240}
tau <- 336
n_dose <- 26
dose_times <- (seq_len(n_dose) - 1) * tau
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0, n_dose * tau, by = 24),
                           dose_times + 0.5, dose_times + 2)))

make_events <- function(cohort, amt_fun) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohort)), function(i) {
    cv <- cohort[i, ]
    dose <- data.frame(id = cv$id, time = dose_times, amt = amt_fun(cv),
                       dur = 0.5, evid = 1, cmt = "central")
    obs <- data.frame(id = cv$id, time = obs_times, amt = 0, dur = 0,
                      evid = 0, cmt = "central")
    bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
      mutate(ALB = cv$ALB, CRCL = cv$CRCL, WT = cv$WT)
  })) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

ev_240 <- make_events(cohort, function(cv) 240)
sim_240 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev_240, returnType = "data.frame"))

vpc_240 <- sim_240 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r fig-vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated nivolumab serum concentrations after 240 mg every 2 weeks (median and 90% prediction interval, 200 virtual patients). Compare with the concentration range in Figure 3 of Tohi 2023 (a pcVPC of the observed data, which this simulation cannot reproduce point for point)."}
ggplot(vpc_240, aes(time / 24, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5, linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(x = "Time since first dose (days)", y = "Nivolumab (ug/mL)",
       caption = "Dotted line: assay LLOQ 5 ug/mL") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Replicating Figure 1: covariate effects on clearance

Figure 1 plots the individual post hoc CL against albumin, eGFR and time
since the first dose, with the final-model typical CL overlaid. The typical
curves are reproduced below from the model's own `cl` output.

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Typical nivolumab clearance versus albumin (at eGFR 70, t = 0), eGFR (at albumin 3.6 g/dL, t = 0) and time since the first dose (at the reference covariates). Replicates the solid lines of Figure 1A-C of Tohi 2023."}
typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
one_cl <- function(alb_gdL, egfr, time) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = seq_along(alb_gdL), time = time, amt = 0, evid = 0,
                   cmt = "central", ALB = alb_gdL * 10, CRCL = egfr)
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(typ, ev, returnType = "data.frame"))$cl
}
alb_grid <- seq(2.5, 4.8, by = 0.05)
egfr_grid <- seq(29, 144, by = 1)
time_grid <- seq(0, 1217 * 24, by = 24)
fig1 <- bind_rows(
  tibble(panel = "A: albumin (g/dL)", x = alb_grid,
         cl = one_cl(alb_grid, rep(70, length(alb_grid)), rep(0, length(alb_grid)))),
  tibble(panel = "B: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)", x = egfr_grid,
         cl = one_cl(rep(3.6, length(egfr_grid)), egfr_grid, rep(0, length(egfr_grid)))),
  tibble(panel = "C: time since first dose (days)", x = time_grid / 24,
         cl = one_cl(rep(3.6, length(time_grid)), rep(70, length(time_grid)), time_grid))
)
ggplot(fig1, aes(x, cl)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Typical CL (L/h)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig1-check}
# The model's cl must equal the printed final CL equation evaluated by hand;
# both sides use the same numbers, so the bound is numerical tolerance only.
by_hand <- function(alb, egfr, t) {
  0.0064 * (alb / 3.6)^-1.48 * (egfr / 70)^0.411 *
    exp(-0.285 * t^2.02 / (1510^2.02 + t^2.02))
}
chk <- data.frame(alb = c(2.5, 3.6, 4.8, 3.6), egfr = c(30, 70, 144, 70),
                  t = c(0, 0, 2000, 8760))
chk$model <- mapply(one_cl, chk$alb, chk$egfr, chk$t)
chk$hand <- with(chk, by_hand(alb, egfr, t))
knitr::kable(chk, digits = 6)
stopifnot(all(abs(chk$model / chk$hand - 1) < 1e-8))
```

# Replicating Figure S1: Monte Carlo trough concentrations

The authors simulated steady-state trough concentrations (Css,min) for
240 mg and 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks at albumin 2.5, 3.5 and 4.5 g/dL and eGFR
30, 60, 90 and 120 mL/min/1.73 m$^2$, and plotted them as boxplots (Figure
S1). The medians below were digitised by the maintainers from Figure S1;
the two extremes agree with the values stated in the Discussion (26.7 and
231.6 ug/mL), which are used directly for those two cells.

Because clearance keeps decreasing with time, the timing of "steady state"
matters. The paper does not state it. Troughs are taken here at the end of
the 26th dosing interval (one year, when the time effect on CL has reached
97% of its maximum) and, as a sensitivity, at the end of the 12th
(24 weeks).

```{r figS1-ref}
figS1_ref <- tribble(
  ~regimen,  ~alb, ~egfr, ~cmin_ref,
  "3 mg/kg", 2.5,  30,  61.7,
  "3 mg/kg", 2.5,  60,  41.2,
  "3 mg/kg", 2.5,  90,  31.9,
  "3 mg/kg", 2.5, 120,  26.7,
  "3 mg/kg", 3.5,  30, 113.2,
  "3 mg/kg", 3.5,  60,  81.0,
  "3 mg/kg", 3.5,  90,  65.2,
  "3 mg/kg", 3.5, 120,  55.8,
  "3 mg/kg", 4.5,  30, 174.0,
  "3 mg/kg", 4.5,  60, 126.0,
  "3 mg/kg", 4.5,  90, 102.6,
  "3 mg/kg", 4.5, 120,  93.3,
  "240 mg",  2.5,  30,  82.2,
  "240 mg",  2.5,  60,  55.3,
  "240 mg",  2.5,  90,  43.0,
  "240 mg",  2.5, 120,  37.1,
  "240 mg",  3.5,  30, 151.8,
  "240 mg",  3.5,  60, 106.7,
  "240 mg",  3.5,  90,  86.8,
  "240 mg",  3.5, 120,  75.1,
  "240 mg",  4.5,  30, 231.6,
  "240 mg",  4.5,  60, 169.3,
  "240 mg",  4.5,  90, 138.3,
  "240 mg",  4.5, 120, 123.7
) |>
  mutate(treatment = sprintf("%s, ALB %.1f, eGFR %d", regimen, alb, egfr))
```

```{r figS1-sim}
n_per_arm <- 200
scen <- figS1_ref |>
  select(regimen, alb, egfr, treatment) |>
  mutate(scen = row_number())
wt_draw <- rtnorm(n_per_arm, 59.7, 12.3, 30, 120)

# One interval at the start and the 12th and 26th intervals are sampled
# densely enough for PKNCA; no dose is given after the 26th interval, so its
# end-of-interval sample is a clean trough.
nca_grid <- c(0, 0.5, 2, 6, 24, 48, 96, 168, 240, 336)
intervals_nca <- tibble(
  start = c(0, 11 * tau, 25 * tau),
  end = c(tau, 12 * tau, 26 * tau),
  window = c("Dose 1", "Dose 12", "Dose 26")
)
ev_s1 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(k) {
  ids <- (k - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  amt <- if (scen$regimen[k] == "240 mg") rep(240, n_per_arm) else 3 * wt_draw
  dose <- data.frame(id = rep(ids, each = n_dose), time = rep(dose_times, n_per_arm),
                     amt = rep(amt, each = n_dose), dur = 0.5, evid = 1)
  obs_t <- unique(unlist(lapply(intervals_nca$start, function(s) s + nca_grid)))
  obs <- data.frame(id = rep(ids, each = length(obs_t)),
                    time = rep(obs_t, n_per_arm), amt = 0, dur = 0, evid = 0)
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", ALB = scen$alb[k] * 10, CRCL = scen$egfr[k],
           treatment = scen$treatment[k])
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_s1 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev_s1, keep = "treatment",
                                        returnType = "data.frame"))
```

```{r figS1-plot, fig.cap = "Simulated trough concentrations at the end of the 26th dosing interval by regimen, albumin and eGFR (boxes: 200 virtual patients per cell); crosses are the medians digitised from Figure S1 of Tohi 2023."}
trough <- sim_s1 |>
  filter(time %in% c(12 * tau, 26 * tau)) |>
  left_join(scen, by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(window = ifelse(time == 26 * tau, "Dose 26", "Dose 12"))

ggplot(filter(trough, window == "Dose 26"),
       aes(factor(egfr), Cc, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_point(data = figS1_ref, aes(factor(egfr), cmin_ref, group = regimen),
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("ALB =", alb)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 450)) +
  labs(x = "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)", y = "Css,min (ug/mL)", fill = "Dose") +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA computes Cmax, Cmin, AUC and average concentration over the first,
12th and 26th dosing intervals for every Figure S1 cell. The
`treatment` grouping carries the regimen-albumin-eGFR cell. Cmin of the
first interval is the pre-dose zero; the later intervals' Cmin is the
trough at the end of the interval.

```{r pknca}
conc_s1 <- sim_s1 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
# Guarantee a time-zero record per subject for the first interval.
conc_s1 <- bind_rows(
  conc_s1,
  conc_s1 |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, time)

dose_s1 <- ev_s1 |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_s1, Cc ~ time | treatment + id,
                             concu = "ug/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_s1, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
                             doseu = "mg")
intervals <- intervals_nca |>
  select(start, end) |>
  mutate(cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  left_join(intervals_nca, by = c("start", "end")) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast", "cav")) |>
  group_by(treatment, window, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")

nca_tab |>
  filter(grepl("ALB 3.5, eGFR 60", treatment)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  rename(Treatment = treatment, Window = window,
         "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax, "Cmin (ug/mL)" = cmin,
         "AUC (ug*h/mL)" = auclast, "Cavg (ug/mL)" = cav) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median PKNCA results for the albumin 3.5 g/dL, eGFR 60 cells.")
```

## Comparison against Figure S1

```{r compare}
sim_cmin_26 <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmin", start == 25 * tau) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
ref_cmin <- figS1_ref |>
  select(treatment, cmin = cmin_ref)

tbl <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_cmin_26, ref_cmin,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmin = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(tbl, caption = "Median trough at the end of the 26th dosing interval: Figure S1 of Tohi 2023 (digitised) vs this model.")
attr(tbl, "footnote")
```

```{r compare-gate}
cmp <- trough |>
  group_by(treatment, regimen, alb, egfr, window) |>
  summarise(sim = median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(select(figS1_ref, treatment, cmin_ref), by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / cmin_ref - 1))

cmp |>
  group_by(Window = window) |>
  summarise("Median % diff" = median(pct_diff),
            "Min % diff" = min(pct_diff),
            "Max % diff" = max(pct_diff), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated vs digitised Figure S1 medians, by the trough taken as steady state.")

cmp26 <- filter(cmp, window == "Dose 26")
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed CL, exponent or reference value shifts the
  # whole grid by tens of percent.
  abs(median(cmp26$pct_diff)) < 20,
  quantile(abs(cmp26$pct_diff), 0.9) < 25
)
```

The relative effects stated in the Results can be recomputed from the
simulated medians and compared with the published ranges.

```{r ratios}
med26 <- cmp26 |> select(regimen, alb, egfr, sim)
w <- med26 |> pivot_wider(names_from = regimen, values_from = sim)
reg_pct <- 100 * (w[["240 mg"]] / w[["3 mg/kg"]] - 1)

alb_w <- med26 |> pivot_wider(names_from = alb, values_from = sim, names_prefix = "alb")
alb_vs35 <- 100 * (1 - alb_w$alb2.5 / alb_w$alb3.5)
alb_vs45 <- 100 * (1 - alb_w$alb2.5 / alb_w$alb4.5)

egfr_w <- med26 |> pivot_wider(names_from = egfr, values_from = sim, names_prefix = "e")
e_vs60 <- 100 * (egfr_w$e30 / egfr_w$e60 - 1)
e_vs90 <- 100 * (egfr_w$e30 / egfr_w$e90 - 1)
e_vs120 <- 100 * (egfr_w$e30 / egfr_w$e120 - 1)

ratio_tab <- tibble(
  Comparison = c("240 mg vs 3 mg/kg, % higher",
                 "ALB 2.5 vs 3.5 g/dL, % lower",
                 "ALB 2.5 vs 4.5 g/dL, % lower",
                 "eGFR 30 vs 60, % higher",
                 "eGFR 30 vs 90, % higher",
                 "eGFR 30 vs 120, % higher"),
  Published = c("32.2-38.3", "45.7-51.9", "64.5-71.4", "36.6-49.3", "67.3-93.0", "85.9-129.8"),
  Simulated = sapply(list(reg_pct, alb_vs35, alb_vs45, e_vs60, e_vs90, e_vs120),
                     function(x) sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", min(x), max(x)))
)
knitr::kable(ratio_tab, caption = "Relative differences in median Css,min (Tohi 2023 Results, 'Monte Carlo Simulation Analysis') vs this model.")

# The published ranges come from 1000-patient simulations; allow a few
# percentage points of Monte Carlo noise around each range.
stopifnot(
  median(reg_pct) > 25, median(reg_pct) < 45,
  median(alb_vs35) > 40, median(alb_vs35) < 58,
  median(alb_vs45) > 58, median(alb_vs45) < 78,
  median(e_vs120) > 75, median(e_vs120) < 140
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

## Errata and readings that required arbitration

* **T50 printed as 1501 h in the final CL equation.** Methods ("T50 (1510
  h)") and Table 2 ("1510 (FIX)") both give 1510 h, and the value is
  stated to be taken unchanged from Osawa et al. The final equation in the
  Results prints `1501^2.02`, read here as a transposition. The model uses
  1510 h; the two values change CL by less than 0.5% at any time.
* **Minus signs in the PDF text layer.** The PDF text layer renders the
  minus sign as "2" (e.g. "2 1.48", "2 0.285"); the signs were confirmed on
  the typeset page. The negative albumin exponent also agrees with the text
  ("ALB levels negatively correlated with nivolumab CL").

## Assumptions made because the paper does not say

* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV as CV%. The variances use
  omega$^2$ = log(1 + CV$^2$); reading CV% as 100 x omega instead would give
  0.0376 and 0.214, within the bootstrap 95% CIs either way.
* **Infusion duration.** Not reported; 30 minutes is used.
* **Time origin.** The time-varying CL uses time since the first dose; the
  model reads it from rxode2's `t`, so the first dose must be at time 0.
* **Steady state in the Monte Carlo simulation.** Not defined in the paper.
  The trough at the end of the 26th interval (one year) is the primary
  comparison; its medians run 1-13% above the digitised Figure S1 medians
  (median +6%). The 24-week trough, shown as a sensitivity, agrees with
  Figure S1 to within -12% to +7% (median 0%), so the authors' steady state
  may be earlier than one year. The relative effects of regimen, albumin
  and eGFR match the published ranges at either time. No parameter was
  adjusted to close the gap.
* **Covariate distributions.** Baseline albumin and eGFR are drawn from
  normal distributions with the Table S3 means and SDs, truncated to the
  Table 1 ranges, and held constant over time (Table S3 shows no
  systematic change).
* **Albumin units.** The published coefficient and the reference 3.6 are in
  g/dL; the model takes the canonical `ALB` column in g/L and converts.

## Covariates screened but not retained

Age, body weight, BSA, sex, ECOG performance status, histology and PD-L1
expression were tested on CL and not retained (Table S1; PD-L1 dOFV -3.5,
p = 0.061). They are documented in `covariatesDataExcluded` where a
canonical column exists.

sessionInfo()
